why.text: The challenge requires compensating for soil moisture probe dynamics in an irrigation feedback loop; the company has three seasons of probe and weather data and has already tried a fixed pause without success (C999-CH1).

Nenad Ilić has published on capacitive soil moisture sensor calibration across soil types (SYN-PUB-07491) and long-term field stability assessment of a multi-depth capacitive probe array (SYN-PUB-07495), and holds a granted patent for a multi-depth capacitive soil moisture probe array (SYN-PAT-001).

The researcher has published on sensor-based feedback systems and decision frameworks for precision irrigation (SYN-PUB-07499) and on IoT cloud-based architectures with wireless sensor networks for irrigation scheduling (SYN-PUB-07493, SYN-PUB-07496).
The researcher led WATERWISE, a provincial-funded applied research project delivering a mobile decision support application for irrigation advice across 20 farms (SYN-PRJ-0003).

problem.text: Using the three-season probe and weather archive from C999-CH1, develop a sensor-based feedback decision framework that corrects for probe lag after rainfall, drawing on capacitive sensor calibration methods (SYN-PUB-07491, SYN-PUB-07495, SYN-PAT-001) and sensor-driven irrigation decision logic (SYN-PUB-07499, SYN-PUB-07493) to suppress false irrigation events in the apple orchard controller.

risks.text: SYN-PUB-07491 covers sensor calibration across five Vojvodina soil types in irrigated maize and sunflower plots; SYN-PUB-07495 covers long-term stability in a chernozem profile under irrigated sugar beet and winter wheat; neither record covers orchard conditions, so the company's apple orchard soil may require separate recalibration.

The decision framework record covers field crops in Vojvodina (SYN-PUB-07499), and other irrigation records cover vegetables and sunflower (SYN-PUB-07492, SYN-PUB-07498); none of these records covers perennial tree crops or apple-specific root stress physiology.

why.text: The challenge requires building a predictive model from a multi-year sensor archive; the company has three seasons of probe readings and weather data from 60 hectares (C999-CH1).

Spasoje Orlović has published on time-series feature extraction from environmental sensor data using statistical, wavelet, and autocorrelation-based descriptors (SYN-PUB-02775) and on gradient boosting and random forest classifiers for agronomic event detection on multi-year sensor archives (SYN-PUB-02777, SYN-PUB-02780).
The researcher has published on sensor fusion combining satellite thermal data and ground microclimate networks using Gaussian process regression to estimate crop water stress index (SYN-PUB-02782).
The researcher has published on conformal prediction for uncertainty quantification on temporally autocorrelated environmental sensor data with block-holdout calibration (SYN-PUB-02783).

problem.text: Using the three-season soil moisture probe and weather station archive from C999-CH1, build a predictive model of post-rainfall soil moisture trajectories to detect when the root zone has absorbed sufficient water before the probe equilibrates, drawing on time-series feature extraction from environmental sensor data (SYN-PUB-02775), gradient boosting for agronomic event detection on multi-year sensor archives (SYN-PUB-02777, SYN-PUB-02780), and sensor fusion with Gaussian process regression (SYN-PUB-02782), so the irrigation controller can suppress unneeded events.

risks.text: The published sensor fusion and agronomic event detection records cover field crops and phenological classification; there is no evidence of work on soil moisture probe lag compensation or irrigation control logic for orchards.

The predictive model alone would need to be integrated into the existing irrigation controller; the records cover data analytics pipelines and dashboards (SYN-PRJ-0139), not embedded or real-time irrigation control systems.

why.text: The challenge requires understanding soil water dynamics after rainfall events; the company has three seasons of field probe and weather data (C999-CH1).

Milena Pantelić has published on soil water balance modelling at field scale using CROPWAT with FDR probe verification for soy (SYN-PUB-10776) and AquaCrop calibration and validation with FDR probes for sunflower (SYN-PUB-06983).
The researcher has published on evaluation and comparison of commercial low-cost capacitance soil moisture sensor systems, including accuracy against reference methods (SYN-PUB-06984).

problem.text: Using the three-season probe and weather archive from C999-CH1, calibrate and validate a soil water balance model (CROPWAT or AquaCrop) with FDR probe readings (SYN-PUB-10776, SYN-PUB-06983, SYN-PUB-06984) to characterise post-rainfall soil water redistribution dynamics and define thresholds for a revised irrigation hold signal that avoids root stress in young apple trees.

risks.text: The researcher leads a work package on the SORBWATER project until 2026 and is open only to smaller industrial contracts and consulting aligned with ongoing research (R1047).
The published soil water balance modelling records cover vegetable and field crops; there is no evidence of work on apple orchards or perennial tree root stress physiology.

The published water balance modelling records cover seasonal irrigation scheduling for soy and sunflower; there is no evidence of work on post-rainfall sensor response dynamics or feedback control for irrigation systems.
